subject: surgery
title: Fibroadenoma of the Breast, Breast Mouse, and Phyllodes Tumour

steps.tx: The most common benign breast neoplasm encountered in young women between fifteen and thirty-five years of age is a **fibroadenoma**. Arising from the specialized stromal and epithelial elements of the terminal duct lobular unit, it develops under the hormonal influence of estrogen. Rather than representing a true clonal neoplasm, a fibroadenoma is categorized as an Aberration of Normal Development and Involution (ANDI), characterized by localized hyperplastic overgrowth of glandular epithelium and loose connective tissue.
steps.say: Fibroadenoma is the most common benign breast tumor in young women, developing from terminal duct lobular units as an aberration of normal development driven by estrogen.

vis.alt: Gross pathology photograph of an excised, bisected fibroadenoma of the breast.
vis.caption: Fibroadenoma gross pathology: sharply circumscribed, lobulated, pearly-white oval tumor with slit-like clefts. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: On clinical palpation, a fibroadenoma presents as a solitary, painless, firm, smooth, rubbery, well-circumscribed lump measuring two to three centimetres across. A pathognomonic physical examination hallmark is its extreme mobility within the surrounding breast parenchyma. Because the tumor possesses a delicate pseudo-capsule with no fascial tethering or attachment to surrounding pectoral fascia or overlying skin, it slips freely beneath the examining fingers, earning the famous classical clinical sobriquet of the **breast mouse**.
steps.say: A fibroadenoma presents as a firm, rubbery, well-circumscribed lump. Its remarkable mobility beneath examining fingers earns it the classic moniker of the breast mouse.

vis.alt: Clinical examination photograph demonstrating physical palpation of a mobile breast lump.
vis.caption: Breast examination technique: flat-fingered circular palpation confirming the extreme mobility of a benign fibroadenoma. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Microscopic examination of a fibroadenoma reveals a biphasic proliferation of benign glandular epithelium and proliferating fibrous stroma. Based on architectural patterns, pathologists recognize two classic histological variants: the **intracanalicular pattern and pericanalicular pattern**. In the intracanalicular pattern, proliferating stroma invaginates and compresses ductal lumens into branching, elongated, slit-like clefts. In the pericanalicular pattern, regular concentric rings of fibrous stroma encircle patent, open, rounded glandular ducts.
steps.say: Histology demonstrates a biphasic mix of stroma and epithelium. The intracanalicular pattern compresses ducts into slit-like clefts, while the pericanalicular pattern encircles open ducts.

left.title: Intracanalicular Pattern
points: Stromal proliferation dominates and invaginates ducts
Compresses epithelial lumens into cleft-like slits
Represents classic architecture on low-power microscopy

right.title: Pericanalicular Pattern
points: Fibrous stroma proliferates circumferentially around ducts
Preserves round, patent, open glandular ductal lumens
Dense, collagenous, mature fibrous connective tissue
Often coexists intimately with intracanalicular fields

steps.tx: At high power the two growth patterns sit side by side in one benign biphasic tumour. Stroma squeezing ducts into slits forms the **intracanalicular pattern**, while stroma ringing open round ducts forms the pericanalicular pattern. Both patterns share bland epithelium without atypia, which reassures the pathologist that this mobile lump is a fibroadenoma rather than a phyllodes tumour.
steps.say: Slit-like compressed ducts and round ringed ducts define the two fibroadenoma patterns. Bland epithelium in both keeps this tumour benign.

vis.alt: High-power histology of fibroadenoma showing intracanalicular slit-like ducts and pericanalicular round ducts in fibrous stroma
vis.caption: Fibroadenoma histology showing intracanalicular slit-like ducts beside pericanalicular round ducts in fibrous stroma. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: In postmenopausal women, longstanding fibroadenomas undergo progressive stromal hyalinization, atrophy of epithelial elements, and dystrophic calcification. On screening mammography, these ancient, degenerated fibroadenomas display coarse, chunky, jagged radiopaque calcifications classically described as **popcorn calcification**. These calcifications are entirely benign, requiring no surgical biopsy or intervention, easily distinguished from the fine, branching, pleomorphic microcalcifications characteristic of ductal carcinoma in situ.
steps.say: Ancient fibroadenomas in older women undergo hyalinization and dystrophic calcification, producing coarse popcorn calcifications on mammograms that require no intervention.

left.title: Benign Popcorn Calcifications
points: Completely safe; requires no tissue sampling or excision

right.title: Malignant Pleomorphic Microcalcifications
points: Fine, punctate, branching, linear microcalcifications (<0.5 mm)
Cluster tightly along ductal branches in DCIS
Classified as BI-RADS 4 or 5 (suspicious for malignancy)
Mandates stereotactic vacuum-assisted core needle biopsy

steps.tx: When a fibroadenoma enlarges rapidly during puberty or pregnancy to exceed five centimetres in diameter or five hundred grams in weight, it is designated a **giant juvenile fibroadenoma**. Typically developing in adolescent females between ten and eighteen years of age, it causes alarming unilateral breast asymmetry and stretching of overlying skin with prominent collateral veins. Despite its massive size, it remains histologically benign, managed curatively by surgical enucleation through a circumareolar incision.
steps.say: Giant juvenile fibroadenomas exceed five centimeters during adolescence. Despite rapid growth and alarming breast asymmetry, they are benign and cured by surgical enucleation.

nodes.label: Pubertal Estrogen Surge in Adolescent Female
Rapid Stromal Hyperplasia Exceeds 5 cm Diameter
Complete Enucleation Preserving Native Breast Parenchyma

steps.tx: The critical differential diagnosis of any large or rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial breast mass is a **phyllodes tumour**, historically known as cystosarcoma phyllodes. Like fibroadenoma, it arises from intralobular stroma, but is characterized by marked stromal hypercellularity, leaf-like papillary projections protruding into dilated cystic spaces, and clinical presentation in older women between forty and fifty years. Phyllodes tumours are classified histologically as benign, borderline, or malignant.
steps.say: Phyllodes tumor is the critical differential diagnosis, seen in older women with leaf-like architecture. They range histologically from benign to frankly malignant.

rows: Peak Age Incidence
Young women (15 to 30 years)
Perimenopausal women (40 to 50 years)
Stromal Cellularity
Low cellularity; loose, uniform stromal fibroblasts
Marked stromal hypercellularity with nuclear atypia and mitoses
Architecture
Slit-like or pericanalicular ductal compression
Leaf-like (phyllos) stromal fronds protruding into cystic lumens
Surgical Margins
Simple enucleation along pseudocapsule is curative
Mandates wide local excision with 1 cm clear margins

steps.tx: Malignant phyllodes tumors are distinguished by marked stromal cellular pleomorphism, stromal overgrowth, invasive infiltrative margins, and high mitotic activity exceeding ten mitoses per ten high-power fields. When metastases occur, they disseminate hematogenously to the lungs and bone, while lymph node metastasis occurs in less than one percent. Surgical therapy mandates **wide local excision with a one-centimetre clear margin**, completely avoiding simple enucleation, which leads to high local recurrence.
steps.say: Malignant phyllodes tumors exhibit over ten mitoses per ten fields and spread to the lungs via blood. Wide excision with one centimeter clear margins prevents recurrence.

nodes.label: Core Needle Biopsy Shows Cellular Fibroepithelial Lesion
Wide Local Excision with 1 cm Negative Margins

steps.tx: Standard management for a classic, biopsy-confirmed fibroadenoma measuring less than three centimetres in a young woman under thirty-five is conservative observational surveillance. Because up to one-third of fibroadenomas spontaneously regress or shrink over two to five years, routine excision is unnecessary. Definitive surgical indications include rapid progressive enlargement, size exceeding three to four centimetres, diagnostic uncertainty on core biopsy, or **patient preference for surgical removal**.
steps.say: Small biopsy-proven fibroadenomas in young women are managed conservatively with observation. Surgery is indicated for rapid growth, size over three centimeters, or patient request.

rows: Lesion < 3 cm in Age < 35
Conservative clinical and ultrasound surveillance at 6 and 12 months
One-third regress spontaneously; zero risk of malignant transformation
Rapid Growth or > 4 cm
Surgical enucleation via circumareolar or submammary incision
Excludes phyllodes tumor and prevents cosmetic breast distortion
Complex Fibroadenoma
Complete surgical excision for histological review
Contains cysts >3 mm, sclerosing adenosis, or papillary apocrine changes
